name: AKS Admission and RBAC Persistence
description: Once an attacker can change Kubernetes configuration on AKS, they add things that keep running after they log out: a webhook that injects a sidecar, a CronJob that reconnects, a ClusterRoleBinding that grants them admin, or a service account with a long-lived token. None of that needs a new Azure portal user. The cluster itself becomes the backdoor. Admission webhooks, CronJobs, and role bindings created outside GitOps are the objects to audit.
mitigations: Rotate credentials if the actor is compromised
